Resolves #18107

`#18102` set the policy and landed its first case. This finishes the sweep — **in one change rather than by directory, because the measurement inverted the reason for batching.**

## Deltas

**198 sheets move to `:where()` weight** (99 per neo theme), one line each. `dialog/Base.scss` stays at theme-root in both themes and now carries the comment AC-1 asks for. The guide's clause moves with the code.

**Why not batches.** The ticket's rationale was that *"a sheet's own rules may have relied on (0,2,0) outranking an equal-weight structure rule"*. Measured across all 100 remaining sheets per theme:

```
theme-neo-dark   99 pure-token,  1 mixed   (dialog/Base.scss)
theme-neo-light  99 pure-token,  1 mixed   (dialog/Base.scss)
```

Pure-token means zero non-custom-property declarations and zero nested selectors inside the theme-root rule — nothing that could have been winning a cascade on weight. **That single MIXED result is also the detector's positive control**: a scanner reporting "pure" for everything would be indistinguishable from a broken one.

**And batching was the hazard, not the safeguard.** 23 tokens are declared by more than one sheet in each theme. While some sheets sit at `:where()` and others at theme-root, those tokens change owner by *weight* instead of by load order — so a per-directory sweep would have rewritten the winner for 23 tokens at every step and restored it only at the end. Moving them together is the only arrangement where no token's winner changes at any point.

**The exception, and why it is not a restructure here.** `dialog/Base.scss` nests `.neo-dialog .neo-header-toolbar .neo-button { background-color; height; min-width }` — structural skin that must keep outranking the equal-weight button rules in `src/`. Dropping it to `:where()` would change paint. Per the ticket's own third option it stays at theme-root with a comment naming the rule that keeps it there; the structural half belongs in `src/` per the guide's structure-vs-skin rule, which is a different change with a different blast radius.

## AC Evidence

**AC-1** — every neo value sheet either declares at `:where()` or carries the comment. `grep -rl '^:root .neo-theme-neo-'` over both themes returns exactly the two `dialog/Base.scss` files, and both open with the five-line note.

**AC-2** — the measurement, before and after.

Evidence: themes rebuilt on both trees and every emitted sheet compared.
```
emitted sheets compared : 625
  byte-identical         : 433
  SELECTOR-ONLY change   : 190
  BODY changed           :   2
  present in one tree    :   0
  distinct selector transitions: 2
     :root .neo-theme-neo-dark   ->  :where(.neo-theme-neo-dark)
     :root .neo-theme-neo-light  ->  :where(.neo-theme-neo-light)
```

**The two are `Global.css`, and they are not a body change** — my first comparison split each file at its first `{`, which is wrong for a sheet that emits several rules. Compared properly, the declaration **lists are identical in content and in order**: 267 entries in dark, 265 in light, both trees. Sass grouped the same declarations into more blocks once the selector form changed. No declaration, value or ordering moved anywhere in the tree.

The build ran `-f -n -e esm -t all` with output freshness asserted, because `build-themes` prompts, dies in a non-TTY and **exits 0 without writing** — a stale `dist/` would have made this comparison vacuous in the most convincing way available.

**AC-3** — the guide's subsection no longer describes a sweep in flight. *"Families move to this weight one at a time… while a family still declares at theme-root weight"* becomes one deliberate exception, and the over-specify example narrows from `.neo-tooltip` to `.neo-dialog`, which is the only family it still applies to.

## Test Evidence

`check-theme-value-files`, `check-theme-coverage` and `check-theme-surfaces` exit 0; the first two and `check-relative-links` also ran through `lint-staged` across all 201 staged files.

**What this evidence does not cover, stated rather than implied:** emitted CSS is not the computed cascade. Byte-identical declarations prove the sheets are unchanged; they do not by themselves prove paint is unchanged. What carries that is the pair of *before* measurements — pure-token sheets have no rule that could have been winning on weight, and moving every sheet together means no token's winner changes. I took no rendered screenshot; if a reviewer wants one for a named family, ask and I will add it rather than argue the inference is sufficient.

## Post-Merge Validation

- **`dialog/Base.scss`'s structural rule belongs in `src/`** and is the one piece of `#18107` this PR deliberately leaves standing. It is documented in the file and in the guide rather than ticketed, per the operator's standing instruction to reduce rather than grow the backlog; it earns a ticket when someone picks up the restructure.
- **Consumer bridges retire per family** per the ticket's non-goals. The Workstation's `body:has()` rules are untouched here; each can now go, since every family it bridges has moved.
- The 23 multi-sheet token declarations are worth knowing about independently of this change — they mean load order decides those winners now that weight no longer does.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: `:where()` is specificity zero, so these tokens move from `(0,2,0)` to `(0,0,0)`. That is the intent — themes become overridable — but it is a **public-facing behavioural change for consumers**, not only an internal weight tidy. An app that today overrides a neo token with a plain class selector loses to the theme sheet and will now win. That is almost always what the consumer wanted, and silent when it flips.

  The guide now tells a *projecting* author what to do, which covers the forward case. What I could not find is anything that tells an **existing** consumer their overrides may start taking effect after upgrading. Not a blocker and not this PR's job to fix — but worth a release-note line, and I would rather name it than let it arrive as a surprise bug report against a theme sheet.

  Also verified and clean: `design-tokens/Core.scss` and the covid header sheets use `#{color.adjust(...)}` interpolation inside token values. My first scan read those braces as nested selectors and produced **twelve false positives**; the corrected scan, with interpolation stripped, returns zero. Recording that because the naive detector is the one a future reviewer will reach for, and it will lie in the same direction.
